reason: The sources robustly corroborate through multiple independent sites that orbital weightlessness is free fall rather than absent gravity, along with its mechanics and physiological consequences.
story: Astronauts floating weightlessly aboard the International Space Station are not in a zero-gravity void. Orbiting roughly 250 miles above Earth, gravity is still nearly 90 percent as strong as on the ground. Spacecraft remain in orbit because they are hurtling sideways at immense speeds, about 17,500 miles per hour, while continuously plummeting toward Earth. The planet's surface curves away just as fast as the ship falls, locking the vehicle and its crew into perpetual free fall. What vanishes is not gravity, but apparent weight: the contact force from a floor or seat pushing back against your body. Because the astronaut, the walls, and the air all drop at the exact same rate, floating is essentially an unending downward drop that never hits bottom. Sustained free fall tricks human biology, prompting body fluids to rush to the head and causing muscles and bones to waste away.
angle: Astronauts aboard the space station are not floating in zero gravity; they are plunging toward Earth nonstop under nearly full planetary gravity, but moving sideways so fast that they constantly miss the planet.

claims.claim: Weightlessness in orbit is not caused by the absence of gravity, as Earth's gravity still extends strongly into space.
Orbiting spacecraft and astronauts are in a perpetual state of free fall around Earth.
Astronauts appear to float because they and their spacecraft are accelerating downward toward Earth at the exact same rate.
At a typical space station orbital altitude of approximately 400 kilometers, Earth's gravity is still around 89 percent of its surface strength, or about 8.7 meters per second squared.
Sensations of weight originate from contact forces, such as floors or seats pushing against the body, rather than gravity itself.
Apparent weight drops to zero in free fall because there is no normal supporting force pushing back on the body.
Satellites stay in orbit because immense horizontal speed causes Earth's curved surface to drop away as fast as the satellite falls.
Scientists prefer the term microgravity because tiny accelerations of about one-millionth of a g remain on spacecraft due to atmospheric drag, structural vibrations, and crew movement.
Specially modified aircraft flying parabolic arcs create brief periods of weightlessness lasting approximately 20 to 30 seconds.
The 1995 feature film Apollo 13 filmed weightless flight scenes aboard parabolic aircraft.
Ground-based drop facilities like NASA's Zero Gravity Research Facility achieve roughly 5 seconds of weightless free fall in an evacuated chamber.
Roller coaster drops and drop rides temporarily produce the exact same sensation of weightlessness as orbital free fall.
Without the mechanical load of gravity, astronauts experience bone mineral loss and muscle mass atrophy.
In weightlessness, fluids shift upward toward the chest and head, causing facial puffiness and reduced fluid volume in the legs.
Space motion sickness and disorientation affect nearly half of all space travelers due to sensory conflict in the vestibular system.
Astronauts on the International Space Station typically exercise around two hours each day to combat musculoskeletal decay.
Valeri Polyakov set the record for the longest continuous stay in space at nearly 438 days.
Long-duration spaceflight causes physiological changes in astronauts' eyes, including shifts toward farsightedness and flattened eyeballs.

disputed: The underlying cause of astronaut vision changes remains unproven: some researchers cite elevated cabin carbon dioxide while others point to upward cerebrospinal fluid pressure or homocysteine levels; scripts should state that the exact trigger is still under investigation.
Parabolic weightlessness duration varies by aircraft and profile between 20 and 30 seconds; scripts should qualify the duration as approximately 20 to 30 seconds per arc.

Sources differ on whether bone density loss is nearly solved via resistive equipment and drugs or remains an ongoing severe hazard; scripts should attribute optimistic claims about defeating bone loss as preliminary.
